title: D-FINE vs RF-DETR: full benchmark comparison
dek: Measured on one COCO protocol on an RTX 5070 Ti: D-FINE averages 7.5 mAP points higher at matched compute, while RF-DETR runs 35.8% faster.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: On an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, D-FINE averages 7.5 mAP points higher than RF-DETR at matched parameter counts, winning both nearest-params pairings. The trade is speed: RF-DETR runs 35.8% faster on average. D-FINE leads on accuracy from the smallest variant to the largest, so pick it for accuracy and RF-DETR for throughput.

D-FINE fields 5 measured variants and RF-DETR fields 4, all on the same COCO val2017 protocol on an RTX 5070 Ti. RF-DETR's variants cluster between 30 and 34M parameters, so only 2 pairings match closely by parameter count.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017, D-FINE and RF-DETR variants highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent. The comparison pairs each D-FINE variant with the nearest RF-DETR variant by parameter count. Across those 2 pairings D-FINE averages 7.5 mAP points higher and wins both. At the top end D-FINE-X reaches 61.4 mAP against RF-DETR-L at 58.6. At the small end D-FINE-N is a 3.78M model at 45.8 mAP, far lighter than RF-DETR's smallest at 30.47M and 51.4 mAP.
Averaged across the matched pairs, RF-DETR is 35.8% faster than D-FINE in PyTorch, and its lead grows with model size.

Pick D-FINE when you want the most accuracy per parameter: it leads at both matched sizes and reaches 61.4 mAP at the top. Pick RF-DETR when throughput is the constraint, since it runs 35.8% faster on average in this pairing. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the call.
